newsitem.title: USA: Hewlett-Packard third-quarter net less than expected.
newsitem.headline: Hewlett-Packard third-quarter net less than expected.

text.p: Hewlett-Packard Co. on Monday reported fiscal third-quarter net income that was less than Wall Street expected because of slow medical equipment sales and higher costs.

The second-largest computer company reported net income of $617 million, or 58 cents a share, compared with $425 million, or 40 cents, in the same quarter a year ago. Revenue for the quarter ended July 31 rose 15 percent to $10.5 billion from $9.11 billion a year earlier.
Wall Street expected Hewlett-Packard, based in Palo Alto, Calif., to earn 68 cents a share, according to a recent analyst survey by First Call.
"Our results this quarter were mixed," said Lewis Platt, H-P chairman and chief executive.
Strong sales in computer systems, printer supplies and semiconductor test equipment were offset by shipment delays in medical equipment and high costs, Platt said.
The company has several key product introductions in the works and will roll out new services, but it also has to bring its expenses into line, Platt said.
